title: Festivals, Europe and how few musicians live from jazz
summary: Hodes says jazz festivals and Europe opened up. He cites Davern's five percent figure.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I suddenly found out that I wasn't going to get anything back, I was going to give them more. But it was a good feeling. All this came through these TV shows, admittedly so. But there was also movement. Jazz was becoming more -- there was an audience growing up and there was things going on in jazz all over the country. There was something in Colorado going on, there was something in Odessa, Texas, there was something in Decatur, there's something in Manassas. There are suddenly festivals.

And then the European scene opened up. And all this helped make for more work for a select few musicians. Like our friend Kenny Davern says, five percent of the musicians in the country are making a livelihood out of music. Now, take that five percent and figure out how many of them are jazz musicians. And you will find that in New York City, if you find 50 you've found quite a few that are making it strictly playing jazz. And in Chicago, two, three, one, four, how many? Playing jazz. I'm not thinking about --
Yeah, I'm not thinking about the fellow that appears in the studio --
Well, some guys are doing nothing but playing jazz but they're not doing too well.
This is what I -- yeah. It's a hanging-
on thing, you're just making enough paper. So this is the story. But it -- still, it's gotten better for a few.
